data.long_meaning: The name Uzzias is derived from the Hebrew roots 'ez' meaning 'help' and 'yah' meaning 'God'. In the Old Testament, Uzzias was a king of Judah who ruled wisely and justly, bringing prosperity and peace to his people. His name reflects his dependence on God for strength and guidance. The name Uzzias carries the meaning “God of help” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Uzzias usually hope their child will grow to embody god of help and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Uzzias, which means 'God's help', was popular among the Hebrews. It reflected their belief in God as a source of strength and support in times of need. Uzzias, as a king, embodied this belief, ruling with wisdom and justice that brought prosperity and peace to his people. The name became a symbol of reliance on divine assistance and was passed down through generations.
data.spiritual_significance: For a Christian, the name Uzzias carries a deeper spiritual significance. It serves as a reminder of God's presence and role as ourhelp in all aspects of life. It encourages us to trust in God's plan and guidance, rather than relying on our own strength and wisdom. The name calls us to pray for help and support in times of need, and to give thanks for God's provision and protection in our lives. Furthermore, the life of King Uzzias, who ruled with wisdom and justice, is a model for how we, as Christians, should strive to live our lives in accordance with God's will.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Uzzias, meaning "strength of God," is a name that signifies divine empowerment. It encourages the bearer to tap into the limitless power of God, relying on God's strength to overcome challenges and achieve greatness.

biblical_reference.note: Uzzias was the name of a king of Judah in the biblical book of 2 Chronicles, chapter 26, verse 16.

historical_references.reference: Uzziah, also known as Azariah, was the fifteenth king of Judah, ruling from approximately 783 to 742 BCE. He was the son of Jotham and was succeeded by Jotham's brother, Ahaz. Uzziah is considered one of the 'great' kings of Judah due to his faithfulness to God and his military successes.

Uzziah is also mentioned in the Old Testament as a priest who rebuilt the altar at the North Gate of the Temple in Jerusalem during the reign of King Josiah. The rebuilding of the altar was significant because it was a symbol of the people's renewed commitment to God and the covenant. This event occurred around 622 BCE.
